asks: How does Silo know that lines are missing?
answer: Every source numbers what it writes, before sending. A missing number is a gap, which the recorder writes as a fact, since it saw the hole itself. A source that restarts says so and starts a new count, so that a restart neither reads as a loss nor hides one. A source with nothing to say sends its last number from time to time, so that a loss at the end shows. A number that arrives twice is written once.
